title: Japanese PM visits Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae laid a wreath on the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at the Libingan ng mga Bayani in Taguig City on Wednesday.

blocks.text: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae laid a wreath on the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at the Libingan ng mga Bayani in Taguig City on Wednesday.
Takaichi is in the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, where she participated in several meetings with other world leaders.

“On November 18, commencing at 10:50 a.m. local time (11:50 a.m. Japan time), for approximately 10 minutes, Ms. Takaichi Sanae, Prime Minister of Japan, who is visiting the Philippines, visited the Heroes’ Cemetery and laid a wreath at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan said in a short statement.
According to the Armed Forces of the Philippines, the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is dedicated to unidentified soldiers who died in the war.
It lies at the center of the Libingan ng mga Bayani with a simple plaque saying “Here lies a Filipino soldier whose name is known only to God.”
The statue serves as a monument where government officials and dignitaries would often conduct wreath-laying ceremonies.

“More than a monument, it stands as a solemn reminder of the countless Filipino soldiers whose identities may have been lost, but whose courage, sacrifice, and service to the nation will never be forgotten,” the AFP said in an X post in August.
During the Japanese occupation of the Philippines in World War II, thousands of Filipino soldiers and civilians were killed.
Japanese soldiers forced 70,000 to 76,000 Filipino and American soldiers to march 100 kilometers in what is now known as the Bataan Death March.
While historical accounts vary, thousands of soldiers died during the march due to hunger and exhaustion. –NB, GMA News
